Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that there is limited evidence to suggest that global management at the same center improves results for patients with colorectal cancer and synchronous liver metastases.

One study (Prompt Completion) found that Global Management of CRC and SLM was associated with fewer procedures but did not influence overall survival. This suggests that more rigorous selection of patients for surgery, possibly through better staging or identification of high-risk lesions, may contribute to improved outcomes after surgical resection of the synchronous liver metastases.

Another study (Prompt Completion) discovered that SM was associated with a longer delay and increased use of chemotherapy between procedures, indicating that managing this condition might require more careful consideration of patient selection and treatment optimization to achieve better results.
